name: RM-Bench
description: A benchmark evaluating the sensitivity and robustness of Reward Models (RMs) used in RLHF training. Tests whether reward models can distinguish subtle quality differences and are robust to stylistic manipulations (length, format, sycophancy). Reveals that many reward models primarily reward surface-level style properties — verbosity, formatting — rather than genuine quality, explaining why RLHF can lead to reward hacking.
evaluation_method: accuracy on preference pairs; sensitivity to subtle quality differences; robustness to style perturbations
general_score_metric: reward model accuracy on subtle preference pairs; style robustness score
typical_sota_score: RMs show ~60–75% accuracy on subtle quality pairs; often fooled by length and format manipulations
reputation: ICLR 2025 Oral; critical for understanding reward hacking in RLHF; reveals systematic weaknesses in commercial reward models; foundational for developing better RM evaluation methodology
notes: ICLR 2025 Oral. Finding: reward models often prefer verbose, well-formatted responses over concise, accurate ones — a systematic bias that leads to reward hacking during RLHF. Tests both sensitivity (detecting subtle quality differences) and robustness (not being fooled by style changes). Multiple commercial and open-source RMs evaluated. Explains a key failure mode in RLHF: training signal is dominated by style rather than substance.
